solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wrong to allow pub by ancient monument

indicators.note: to allow in is to admit, so the word for wrong lets the pub inside it

parts.note: a wrong is a sin
PH is the map abbreviation for public house
X is the multiplication sign, read 'by' as in three by four

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark that a pub should never have been allowed to open beside a historic monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to allow' works as a container: to allow in is to let inside. 'by' gives X, as in measurements like three by four.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Sphinx at Giza is a famous monument of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Crawling outside in manoeuvres converted troops

indicators.note: converted means turned round, so the picked pair of letters is turned back to front
the outside letters in the word manoeuvres are its first and last

parts.note: troops collectively form an army

explanation.surface: Soldiers on exercises who have changed sides, crawling about in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawling' looks like soldiers moving on their bellies, but means fawning; 'converted' signals turning round.
explanation.definitionFit: Crawling in the sense of fawning or ingratiating, which is how an oily, obsequious person behaves.

clue.text: Novelist keeping pottery in quarters during literary festival

indicators.note: during means the other letters sit within the festival's name

parts.note: Hay-on-Wye in Wales hosts the famous Hay literary festival

indicators.note: the pottery sits in between the two quarter letters

parts.note: E and W, east and west, are two quarters or compass points
Ming is the Chinese porcelain of the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: A writer storing some pottery in his lodgings while attending a book festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Hay-on-Wye is a Welsh book town with a famous annual festival. 'keeping' simply links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was the American author of novels such as The Old Man and the Sea.

clue.text: Grey squirrel finally tracks nut — with ear, unusually

indicators.note: tracks means follows behind, so the last letter of squirrel comes after the rest
unusually signals that the letters of nut and ear appear in an unusual order
finally picks the closing letter of squirrel

explanation.surface: A grey squirrel tracking down a nut by ear, which is unusual behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges NUT and EAR into NEUTRA. 'Grey' looks like it describes the squirrel but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutral colour is a muted, unsaturated one such as grey or beige.

clue.text: Talk with salesman before meal to redirect carrier

indicators.note: to redirect is to send back the way it came, so the whole string runs backwards

parts.note: to gab is to talk idly
a rep is a sales representative
a.p. abbreviates ante prandium, Latin for before a meal, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Chatting with a salesman before dinner about rerouting a delivery firm.
explanation.walkthrough: GAB, REP and AP run together and the whole string read backwards gives the answer. AP, ante prandium, is a pharmacist's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper sack with handles is something for carrying shopping, so it is a carrier.

clue.text: Mythical hero a seaman's mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the answer is how the phrase sounds when said

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, so a seaman's is a jack's

explanation.surface: A legendary hero turns out to be the one a sailor talks about.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, as in Jack Tar, is slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a Greek warrior of the Trojan War in legend, famed for his strength.

clue.text: Entangle ball in tree, when climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed
the ball goes in the tree's name

parts.note: a lime is a linden tree
an orb is a ball or sphere

explanation.surface: A ball has got caught up in a tree while someone climbs to fetch it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when climbing' turns LIORBME upwards, as the entry is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to involve them in a conflict, so they become entangled in it.

clue.text: Toff, framing lines, going back

indicators.note: in a down entry going back means the letters read upwards, reversed
framing means surrounding, so the toff goes round the lines

parts.note: a nob is a toff, an upper-class person
RY is the abbreviation for railway lines

explanation.surface: An aristocrat composing verse and harking back to the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns NORYB round. The whole clue also describes the poet: a lord (a toff) who wrote lines and belongs to the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Byron was an aristocratic Romantic poet, so a titled writer of verse from long ago.

clue.text: Wine ingredient explosive, needing check over day

indicators.note: the explosive needs the check put over the day, replacing that letter
the explosive needs the check put over the day, replacing that letter

parts.note: a grenade is a small explosive bomb
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: A recipe-like claim that a wine ingredient is explosive and must be checked after a day.
explanation.walkthrough: In GRENADE, the D (day) is replaced by CH (check).
explanation.definitionFit: Grenache is a red grape variety, widely used in Rhône and Spanish wines.

clue.text: Protection Romeo used during love affair

indicators.note: used during means placed in the middle of the love affair word

parts.note: an amour is a love affair
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A frank remark about Romeo using protection during an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside AMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Armour is the metal covering that shields a soldier, so it gives protection.

clue.text: Brownies might be among this confectionery carried back to house

parts.note: jam is a sweet preserve, loosely confectionery
bore is the past tense of bear, to carry

indicators.note: back to picks the last letter of house

explanation.surface: Chocolate brownies might be found in a box of sweets brought back to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are not cakes here but junior Girl Guides, the young members of the Guide movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large rally of Scouts and Guides, so Brownies might attend one.

clue.text: Artist sculpted prima donna unclothed

indicators.note: sculpted means shaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
unclothed strips off the outer covering, the first and last letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: An artist making a nude sculpture of an opera star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prima donna' without its outer P and A leaves RIMADONN, which 'sculpted' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Piet Mondrian was a Dutch painter famed for grids of primary colours.

clue.text: Ancient Donegal's missing Norse ruins

indicators.note: ruins means wrecks, so the remaining letters are jumbled
missing means lacking, so one letter is taken out

parts.note: the county name, with 's read as is
N is the abbreviation for Norse

explanation.surface: An ancient site in County Donegal lacks the Norse ruins one might expect.
explanation.walkthrough: DONEGAL without N gives DOEGAL, which 'ruins' rearranges. Donegal is a county in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something age-old has existed for a very long time, so it is ancient.

clue.text: Time to leave musical instrument with Academy that's near the pupil

indicators.note: to leave means the time letter departs from the instrument

parts.note: a cornet is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: A school scene: time for a pupil to leave music class with his instrument for the Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' suggests a schoolchild but means the opening in the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the transparent layer at the front of the eye, lying just over the pupil.

clue.text: Runaway leader in relay, Suzanne regularly enters races

indicators.note: enters means goes inside, so these letters are placed within the races

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle races

indicators.note: the leader in relay is its first letter
regularly picks every other letter of Suzanne

explanation.surface: A sports report: a relay runner named Suzanne regularly enters races.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle races; 'regularly' takes the even letters of Suzanne.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant is a child who runs away from school, so a runaway.

clue.text: Shakespeare's contemporary Lear: regal, with suffering

indicators.note: suffering means in torment, so the letters are distorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Describes King Lear: regal, yet suffering, as in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: LEAR, REGAL and WITH are rearranged together; 'with' is part of the anagram, not a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Raleigh, Elizabethan courtier and explorer, lived at the same time as the playwright.

clue.text: Dean perhaps arranged rite to embrace Church music

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold inside, so the rearranged letters surround the rest
arranged means put in a new order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
ska is a Jamaican music style

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean arranging a church rite with music.
explanation.walkthrough: RITE rearranged gives ITER, which embraces CE and SKA. Christopher Dean won Olympic ice dance gold with Jayne Torvill.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Dean is a famous example of a skater on ice, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Beware! It's no good infiltrating London area to look for scraps

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so these letters go within the London district

parts.note: SE is a London postal district, South East
cave is Latin for beware, old school slang for look out

explanation.surface: A warning that useless people are infiltrating part of London to scavenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cave!' was the public-school lookout's warning, from Latin. 'It's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To scavenge is to search through refuse for anything usable.

clue.text: Party calls to arrange card for exhibition centre

indicators.note: to arrange means to put in order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A party organiser calls to arrange an invitation card for an exhibition venue.
explanation.walkthrough: PARTY, CALLS and ACE are rearranged together. The Crystal Palace was built in Hyde Park, London, for the Great Exhibition of 1851.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crystal Palace was the glass hall housing the 1851 Great Exhibition.

clue.text: Quite elevated golf commentator contracted to occupy perimeter of twelfth

indicators.note: to occupy means to sit inside, so the shortened name goes within the perimeter letters
the perimeter of twelfth is its first and last letters
contracted means shortened, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Peter Alliss was the BBC's long-serving golf commentator

explanation.surface: A golf commentator signed up to work around the twelfth hole, which is on high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Alliss was the BBC's voice of golf for decades; 'contracted' drops his final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallish means fairly tall, so somewhat raised or elevated.

clue.text: Bathroom accessory's available in gold, mum, if really necessary

indicators.note: available in means found inside, so the accessory sits within the gold symbol

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a tap is a bathroom fitting; the 's is read as is
mum as in keep mum means silence, so sh

explanation.surface: A shop note: this bathroom fitting comes in gold, Mum, if you really must.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not a mother here but silence, as in keeping mum.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning only under pressure or in an emergency.

clue.text: Animated sources of film revealed by independent broadcaster

indicators.note: the sources of the words film and revealed are their first letters

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: The origins of an animated film are disclosed by an independent TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animated' suggests cartoons, but here means lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means playful and full of energy, hence lively or animated.

clue.text: Potent sextet cause annoyance

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
to rile is to irritate

explanation.surface: A powerful group of six musicians annoys people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potent' teases a sexual sense, matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Virile means having strength and vigour, especially sexual vigour, so potent.

clue.text: Cosmetic surgeon operated, discarding outer layer

indicators.note: operated means worked on, so the letters are rearranged
discarding the outer layer strips the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A cosmetic surgeon operating and removing a layer of skin.
explanation.walkthrough: SURGEON without its outer S and N leaves URGEO, which 'operated' rearranges. 'Cosmetic' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is a red make-up powder for the cheeks, a cosmetic.

clue.text: Arsenal's chief, extremely tight with money, offloading latest team member

indicators.note: the chief letter of Arsenal's is its first
extremely picks the first and last letters of tight
offloading latest drops the final letter

parts.note: ackers is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A football report: Arsenal's tight-fisted chief sells his newest player.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then TT, then ACKERS without its final S. Arsenal is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: An attacker is a forward, one member of a football side.

clue.text: Rake in bit of cereal over rear of garden

indicators.note: in a down entry over means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: an ear is the grain-bearing head of a cereal plant

indicators.note: the rear of garden is its last letter

explanation.surface: Gardening instructions: rake a scrap of cereal over the back of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' looks like a garden tool but 'Rake in' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rake in money is to gain it in quantity, so to earn.

clue.text: Marine new, showing nervous reaction amongst elements

indicators.note: amongst means in the middle of the element symbols

parts.note: Au and Al are the chemical symbols for gold and aluminium
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A new marine recruit twitching nervously out in the elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elements' gives two chemical symbols, gold and aluminium. 'Marine' looks like a soldier but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical means relating to ships and the sea, so marine.

clue.text: US actor, a name missed from screens

indicators.note: missed from means left out of the word for screens

parts.note: curtains screen a window

explanation.surface: An American film star whose name was left off the screen credits.
explanation.walkthrough: CURTAINS without A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Curtis was a Hollywood film star of Some Like It Hot.

clue.text: Fantastic plane — the Jumbo perhaps

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or wild, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for an aircraft, the Jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests a jet, but Jumbo was a famous circus elephant, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo was a celebrated London Zoo and Barnum circus animal, an example of the species.

clue.text: Hue and cry surrounding that woman

indicators.note: surrounding means placed around, so cry goes round the pronoun

parts.note: her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: A hue and cry raised all around a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hue and cry' reads as a phrase, but 'Hue' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry is a bright red colour, so a hue.
